No genome file? Use a sample
Run one here, or download it and upload it yourself. Two of these are declined on purpose — that is the behaviour, not a fault.
Reduced-function result
Answers confidently
Complete coverage, CYP2C19 *2/*2. Clopidogrel comes back Ineffective — the case this system exists to catch.
Normal result
Answers confidently
Complete coverage, all genes at reference. Shows the system is not merely cautious — it will state when no PGx-guided adjustment was identified from the assessed evidence.
Variants-only file
Declines every gene
The SAME patient as the first sample, with reference rows removed — the common output of most pipelines. The genotype is unchanged; what is lost is the evidence that it was measured.
Real 1000 Genomes sample
Declines every gene
Genuine public research data (NA12273), not synthetic. Polymorphic-filtered, so it is declined — which is what happens to most research VCFs, and why.

results_text:
NA12273 2026-10-14T12:49:23Z VCF accepted 0 variants 1421 ms 23 pipeline warnings The VCF header does not state a reference build; assuming GRCh38. If it is actually GRCh37/hg19, the results will be wrong. Input quality was not established for required positions marked FILTER=. in: CYP2C19 (16), CYP2C9 (17), CYP2D6 (67), DPYD (31), NUDT15 (5), SLCO1B1 (20), TPMT (9). These complete genotypes were retained because the VCF does not explicitly mark them as failed and this application does not invent assay-independent DP/GQ/QUAL thresholds. Confirm the upstream caller's quality policy before relying on them. Every gene (7 of 7) was declined, at 19–57% position coverage. That pattern is a property of the FILE, not of 7 separate genes — and it has two common causes. This looks like a research-format or SNP-array export. • A research VCF (1000 Genomes, gnomAD, most sequencing pipelines) is POLYMORPHIC-FILTERED: it lists only positions where someone differed from the reference. The positions that matched are simply absent, and absent is indistinguishable from never-tested. • A consumer export (23andMe, AncestryDNA) is a GENOTYPING ARRAY, not sequencing. It reports a few hundred thousand chosen positions across the whole genome, which is not the same as reporting every position one gene needs. Neither is a bad file. Both are the wrong shape for this question. What works is a clinical pharmacogenomic panel, or a sequencing pipeline re-run to emit every position including the reference matches. The input requirements page lists the specific sources. DPYD: 8 of 28 positions that could indicate reduced function carry an explicit genotype in this VCF. The gene met its 20% coverage minimum (37%), but percentage is a proxy: a file can clear it while omitting every position capable of showing a variant. Reported as Unknown rather than assuming the missing positions match the reference — which is what would make a reduced-function result read as normal. CPIC gives 3 population-specific recommendations for clopidogrel (CVI ACS PCI, CVI non-ACS non-PCI, NVI). The strongest one is shown (CVI ACS PCI); review the population that matches the patient. clopidogrel: Required genomic evidence is incomplete for CYP2C19. Available partner findings are partial evidence only; no complete drug-level PGx recommendation is made. Pre-generated explanation was not served because its approval or semantic identity did not match (No approval exists for this drug, gene, and phenotype context.) Using the deterministic template. The two lowest activity values (variant activity scores, see CPIC guideline PMID:29152729) are used for unphased data and the lowest activity value per allele is used for phased data to determine the gene activity score and phenotype to retrieve prescribing recommendations. The DPYD gene is on the negative chromosomal strand, all genotype calls for DPYD in this report refer to the positive chromosomal strand. Therefore, genotype calls are complemented from gene bases. The DPYD Reference allele assignment is characterized by the absence of variants at the positions that are included in the underlying allele definitions either because the position is reference or missing. fluorouracil: Required genomic evidence is incomplete for DPYD. Available partner findings are partial evidence only; no complete drug-level PGx recommendation is made. The TPMT gene is on the negative chromosomal strand, all genotype calls for TPMT in this report refer to the positive chromosomal strand. Therefore, genotype calls are complemented from gene bases. The TPMT *1 allele assignment is characterized by the absence of variants at the positions that are included in the underlying allele definitions either because the position is reference or missing. azathioprine: Required genomic evidence is incomplete for TPMT, NUDT15. Available partner findings are partial evidence only; no complete drug-level PGx recommendation is made. The SLCO1B1 genotype (star nomenclature) will be displayed if determinable with the provided VCF based on the SLCO1B1 star allele definition published by CPIC and recommendations are provided based on the genotype.

In case no genotype can be determined, recommendations are based on the rs4149056 genotype alone as per guideline. The minor C allele at rs4149056 defines SLCO1B1*5. The SLCO1B1 *1 allele assignment is characterized by the absence of variants at the positions that are included in the underlying allele definitions either because the position is reference or missing. simvastatin: Required genomic evidence is incomplete for SLCO1B1. Available partner findings are partial evidence only; no complete drug-level PGx recommendation is made. warfarin: No validated automated warfarin-dose implementation is provided by this application; a gene call alone is not a complete dosing recommendation. codeine: CYP2D6 copy-number and structural variation is not called from the uploaded VCF in this application, so codeine guidance is not produced. CYP2D6 structural/copy-number variation cannot be resolved from unphased VCF; outside diplotype input planned explanation mode=static, source=template, guard=n/a (deterministic), slots=verified No qualified clinical expert has reviewed these explanations. Recommendation text is quoted from CPIC annotations issued by PharmCAT; explanatory wording is generated by this application. Automated checks can flag stored wording that does not trace to a CPIC recommendation or a cited mechanism document, but they are not human review and cannot show that every statement is supported: they check provenance, not correctness. No usable pharmacogenomic result for: clopidogrel, fluorouracil, azathioprine, simvastatin, warfarin, codeine. No PGx-guided change Adjust Dosage Toxic Ineffective Unknown

codeine: no pharmacogenomic result (Unknown).
CYP2D6 is a hepatic cytochrome P450 enzyme responsible for metabolising a large share of commonly used drugs. CYP2D6 is unusually variable: as well as single-nucleotide variants that alter or abolish activity, the gene is subject to **whole-gene deletions and duplications**, so copy number differs between people. Activity is conventionally summarised as an activity score derived from both alleles.

Source: Annotation of CPIC Guideline for codeine and CYP2D6 — Crews KR et al. Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium Guideline for CYP2D6, OPRM1, and COMT Genotypes and Select Opioid Therapy. Clin Pharmacol Ther (2021). PMID: 33387367

simvastatin: no pharmacogenomic result (Unknown).
SLCO1B1 encodes OATP1B1, an uptake transporter on the sinusoidal (blood-facing) membrane of liver cells. Its job is to move drugs out of portal blood and into hepatocytes. It is a **transporter, not a metabolising enzyme**, which is why its phenotypes are described as function categories (normal, decreased, poor function) rather than metaboliser categories.
